contentObjective: I can find the percent of a number using an equation or a model.
languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words percent, base, part, and equation.

vocabulary.definition: A part of a number found by multiplying the number by the percent written as a decimal.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una parte de un número que se halla multiplicando el número por el porcentaje escrito como decimal.
vocabulary.cloze: A part found by multiplying a number by a percent in decimal form is the ___ ___ ___ ___.

examples.why: The percent was written as a decimal before multiplying.
Using the percent as a whole number makes it 100 times too big.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.
vocabulary.cloze: A number out of 100 is a ___.

examples.text: 9 out of 100 students walk to school → 9%
examples.why: The comparison is already out of 100.
That is 90%, not 9% — both terms must be scaled to 100.

vocabulary.definition: The whole amount you start with — the number right after the word “of.”
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad total con la que empiezas: el número que va después de la palabra “de”.
vocabulary.cloze: The whole amount you start with, right after the word “of,” is the ___.

examples.why: It is the whole amount, right after the word “of”.

examples.text: The 24 you get as the answer
examples.why: That is the part the percent produced.

vocabulary.definition: How much of the base (the whole) you get. It is your answer.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto obtienes de la base (el total). Es tu respuesta.
vocabulary.visual: 25% of 80 = 20 → the part is 20 (20 out of the 80).
vocabulary.cloze: The amount you get out of the whole is the ___.

examples.why: It is the piece of the base the percent describes.
That is the base, the whole you started from.

vocabulary.definition: A number sentence with an equal sign. The percent one is: part = percent × base.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración numérica con signo de igual. La de porcentaje es: parte = porcentaje × base.
vocabulary.cloze: A number sentence with an equal sign, like part = percent × base, is an ___.

examples.why: Percent times whole equals part, with the unknown whole as n.
The percent relationship multiplies; it never adds.

vocabulary.definition: Money taken off the first price to make it cheaper.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dinero que se quita del precio original para que sea más barato.
vocabulary.cloze: An amount subtracted from a price is a ___.

examples.why: Money taken off the original price.

examples.text: The $60 you pay at the register
examples.why: That is the sale price — what is left after the discount.

vocabulary.definition: Two number lines that line up percents with amounts.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas numéricas que alinean porcentajes con cantidades.
vocabulary.visual: 0%–100% on one line over 0–300 on the other.
vocabulary.cloze: Two lined-up number lines, one for percents and one for amounts, make a ___.

examples.text: A line from 0 to 300 students over a line from 0% to 100%
examples.why: Each amount lines up with its percent.

examples.text: A single number line from 0 to 300
examples.why: One line cannot pair amounts with percents.

vocabulary.definition: A fraction with the same value written with different numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una fracción con el mismo valor escrita con números diferentes.

examples.why: Both the top and bottom were multiplied by 5.
Adding 5 to both parts changes the value.

copyPanel.rule: Finding the Percent of a Number
steps: 1. Identify the percent and the whole (base amount)
2. Convert the percent to a decimal or simplified fraction
3. Multiply the decimal/fraction by the whole to calculate the part

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Book Fair
revealWordProblem.text:
Students were asked which night of the book fair they planned to attend. The results are shown. Then 20% of the students who planned to attend on Wednesday came on Thursday instead, and 25% of the students who planned to attend on Thursday came on Friday instead.
Question: Which day, Thursday or Friday, had the greater actual attendance? How many more students attended that day?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A Book Fair attendance table: Monday 55 students, Tuesday 80, Wednesday 70, Thursday 112, Friday 65.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 20% of Wednesday's 70 students is 0.2 × 70 = 14 students who moved to Thursday, so Thursday's group grows to 112 + 14 = 126. Then 25% of the 112 who had planned Thursday is 0.25 × 112 = 28 students who moved to Friday. Thursday's actual attendance is 126 − 28 = 98, and Friday's is 65 + 28 = 93. Thursday was greater, by 98 − 93 = 5 students.

choiceFeedback: Try converting 20% to a decimal or fraction first.
hints: '20% of 150' means you want a PART of 150 — the answer should be smaller than 150.
Convert the percent to a decimal, then multiply: Part = Percent × Base.
Write 20% as 0.20, then set up 0.20 × 150. (Shortcut: 10% of 150 is 15 — double it.)
hintsEs: '20% de 150' significa que quieres una PARTE de 150: la respuesta debe ser menor que 150.
Convierte el porcentaje en decimal y luego multiplica: Parte = Porcentaje × Base.
Escribe 20% como 0.20 y plantea 0.20 × 150. (Atajo: 10% de 150 es 15; duplícalo.)

choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you subtracted 50 from 84. Instead: Multiply: 0.50 × 84 = ___.
hints: 50% is a friendly percent — it means exactly one-half of the number.
Finding 50% of a number is the same as dividing that number by 2.
Set up 84 ÷ 2, or check with the formula: 0.50 × 84.
hintsEs: 50% es un porcentaje amigable: significa exactamente la mitad del número.
Hallar el 50% de un número es lo mismo que dividir ese número entre 2.
Plantea 84 ÷ 2, o compruébalo con la fórmula: 0.50 × 84.

questions.explanation: 10% = 0.10. Multiply: 0.10 × 320 = 32. (Or move the decimal one place left.)
choiceFeedback: 10% is one-tenth — divide 320 by 10 or move the decimal.
hints: 10% means one-tenth — there's a shortcut that needs no multiplication at all.
To find 10% of any number, move the decimal point one place to the left (divide by 10).
Start with 320 and slide the decimal one place left: 320 → what number?
questions.explanationEs: 10% = 0.10. Multiplica: 0.10 × 320 = 32. (O mueve el punto decimal un lugar a la izquierda.)
hintsEs: 10% significa un décimo: hay un atajo que no necesita ninguna multiplicación.
Para hallar el 10% de cualquier número, mueve el punto decimal un lugar a la izquierda (divide entre 10).
Empieza con 320 y desliza el punto un lugar a la izquierda: 320 → ¿qué número?

reviewHighlights.rule: Finding the Percent of a Number
steps: 1. Identify the percent and the whole (base amount)
2. Convert the percent to a decimal or simplified fraction
3. Multiply the decimal/fraction by the whole to calculate the part
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Find the Percent of a Number is multiplying by the percent number itself instead of its decimal form — for example, finding 30% of 80 by computing 30 × 80 = 2,400 instead of 0.30 × 80 = 24. Always divide the percent by 100 to get the decimal, then multiply that decimal by the base.

hints: Write 50% as 0.5. Then multiply 0.5 by 26.
hintsEs: Escribe 50% como 0.5. Luego multiplica 0.5 por 26.
level1.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.5 × 26 = 13
level1.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.5 × 26 = 13

level1.stem: A book costs $20. It is 10% off. How many dollars do you save?
level1.stemEs: Un libro cuesta $20. Tiene 10% de descuento. ¿Cuántos dólares ahorras?
hints: The base is $20. Write 10% as 0.1 and multiply.
hintsEs: La base es $20. Escribe 10% como 0.1 y multiplica.
level1.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 10 ÷ 100 = 0.1 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.1 × 20 = 2
level1.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 10 ÷ 100 = 0.1 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.1 × 20 = 2

hints: Write 75% as 0.75. Then multiply 0.75 by 24.
hintsEs: Escribe 75% como 0.75. Luego multiplica 0.75 por 24.
level1.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 75 ÷ 100 = 0.75 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.75 × 24 = 18
level1.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 75 ÷ 100 = 0.75 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.75 × 24 = 18

hints: Write 50% as a decimal and multiply by 64. Or find half of 64.
hintsEs: Escribe 50% como decimal y multiplica por 64. O halla la mitad de 64.
level1.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.5 × 64 = 32
level1.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.5 × 64 = 32

hints: The base is 80. Write 15% as 0.15. Then multiply.
hintsEs: La base es 80. Escribe 15% como 0.15. Luego multiplica.
level1.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 15 ÷ 100 = 0.15 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.15 × 80 = 12
level1.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 15 ÷ 100 = 0.15 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.15 × 80 = 12

level2.stem: Theo says 40% of 50 is 2,000, because 40 × 50 = 2,000. What is 40% of 50?
level2.stemEs: Theo dice que el 40% de 50 es 2,000, porque 40 × 50 = 2,000. ¿Cuánto es el 40% de 50?
hints: 40% is less than one whole, so the answer must be less than 50. Write 40% as a decimal first.
hintsEs: El 40% es menos que un entero, así que la respuesta debe ser menor que 50. Primero escribe 40% como decimal.
level2.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 40 ÷ 100 = 0.4 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.4 × 50 = 20
level2.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 40 ÷ 100 = 0.4 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.4 × 50 = 20

hints: Write 35% as a decimal. Multiply it by the base.
hintsEs: Escribe 35% como decimal. Multiplícalo por la base.
level2.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 35 ÷ 100 = 0.35 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.35 × 260 = 91
level2.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 35 ÷ 100 = 0.35 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.35 × 260 = 91

hints: Write 20% as 0.2. Multiply it by the base, 35.
hintsEs: Escribe 20% como 0.2. Multiplícalo por la base, 35.
level2.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 20 ÷ 100 = 0.2 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.2 × 35 = 7
level2.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 20 ÷ 100 = 0.2 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.2 × 35 = 7

level2.stem: How much more is 20% of 150 than 25% of 100?
level2.stemEs: ¿Cuánto más es el 20% de 150 que el 25% de 100?
hints: Find each part first. Then subtract.
hintsEs: Primero halla cada parte. Luego resta.
level2.explanationEs: Halla el 20% de 150: 0.2 × 150 = 30 Halla el 25% de 100: 0.25 × 100 = 25 Resta las partes: 30 − 25 = 5

level2.stem: A bus has 48 seats. 25% of the seats are empty. How many seats are empty?
level2.stemEs: Un autobús tiene 48 asientos. El 25% de los asientos está vacío. ¿Cuántos asientos están vacíos?
hints: The base is 48 seats. 25% is 0.25, or one quarter.
hintsEs: La base es 48 asientos. El 25% es 0.25, o una cuarta parte.
level2.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.25 × 48 = 12
level2.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.25 × 48 = 12

level3.stem: At West Middle School, 45% of the 360 sixth-grade students participate in after-school sports. How many sixth-grade students participate in sports?
choiceFeedback: That is 40% of 360. Multiply by the actual rate: 0.45 x 360.
That is an estimate rather than the exact product. 0.45 x 360 comes to 162.
That is 50% of 360. The rate is 45%, a little less than half.

level3.stem: Ali finds 15% of 70 as 10% plus 5%. Bea multiplies by 0.15. Do they get the same answer? What is 15% of 70?
level3.stemEs: Ali halla el 15% de 70 como 10% más 5%. Bea multiplica por 0.15. ¿Obtienen la misma respuesta? ¿Cuánto es el 15% de 70?
hints: Try both ways. 5% is half of 10%.
hintsEs: Prueba las dos formas. El 5% es la mitad del 10%.
level3.explanation: Ali's way: find 10% and 5%: 0.1 × 70 = 7; 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 Add the two parts: 7 + 3.5 = 10.5 Bea's way: multiply by the decimal: 0.15 × 70 = 10.5
level3.explanationEs: La forma de Ali: halla el 10% y el 5%: 0.1 × 70 = 7; 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 Suma las dos partes: 7 + 3.5 = 10.5 La forma de Bea: multiplica por el decimal: 0.15 × 70 = 10.5

hints: Write 85% as a decimal. Multiply it by the base, 60.
hintsEs: Escribe 85% como decimal. Multiplícalo por la base, 60.
level3.explanation: Write the percent as a decimal: 85 ÷ 100 = 0.85 Multiply the decimal by the base: 0.85 × 60 = 51
level3.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como decimal: 85 ÷ 100 = 0.85 Multiplica el decimal por la base: 0.85 × 60 = 51

level3.stem: Shop A sells a $25 shirt with 8% tax. Shop B sells a $30 shirt with 6% tax. How many dollars more tax does the shirt at Shop A have?
level3.stemEs: La tienda A vende una camisa de $25 con 8% de impuesto. La tienda B vende una camisa de $30 con 6% de impuesto. ¿Cuántos dólares más de impuesto tiene la camisa de la tienda A?
hints: Find the tax at each shop. Then subtract.
hintsEs: Halla el impuesto en cada tienda. Luego resta.
level3.explanation: Find 8% of $25: 0.08 × 25 = 2 Find 6% of $30: 0.06 × 30 = 1.8 Subtract the taxes: 2 − 1.8 = 0.2
level3.explanationEs: Halla el 8% de $25: 0.08 × 25 = 2 Halla el 6% de $30: 0.06 × 30 = 1.8 Resta los impuestos: 2 − 1.8 = 0.2

level3.stem: A school has 80 students. 45% of them play a sport. 25% of those players are on the soccer team. How many students are on the soccer team?
level3.stemEs: Una escuela tiene 80 estudiantes. El 45% practica un deporte. El 25% de esos jugadores está en el equipo de fútbol. ¿Cuántos estudiantes están en el equipo de fútbol?
hints: Find the players first. Then the players are the new base.
hintsEs: Primero halla los jugadores. Luego los jugadores son la nueva base.
level3.explanation: Find 45% of 80: 0.45 × 80 = 36 Use 36 as the new base: 0.25 × 36 = 9
level3.explanationEs: Halla el 45% de 80: 0.45 × 80 = 36 Usa 36 como la nueva base: 0.25 × 36 = 9
